description:
No spec subject

targetRemotes (internal/repo/repo.go:477) probes every remote for refs/heads/beadwork and, when more than one has it, sorts alphabetically and uses the first. The configured remote (bw config remote / git config beadwork.remote) is only consulted in the resolveSingleRemote fallback, which runs only when NO remote has the branch.

Real-world failure: a fork setup with remotes macmorgan, origin (jallum), upstream (own fork), all carrying a beadwork branch, and remote=upstream configured. bw sync picks macmorgan (alphabetically first), tries to push to someone else's repo, and fails with 'permission denied'. If the alphabetically-first remote had been writable, tickets would have been pushed to an unintended repo.

Fix direction: honor the configured remote first whenever it is set and exists, and only fall back to the has-beadwork scan when nothing is configured. The multi-remote warning should become an error (or prompt) rather than a silent alphabetical pick.
title: bw sync ignores configured remote when multiple remotes have the beadwork branch
